findings.issue: After the calldata-decoding loop (whose body allocates), mem[64] is an opaque loop result, and 'v = mem[64]' is never cancelled against later reads of mem[64] although no store to word 64 intervenes. So every call (deployAccessControls ... removeAdmin, grantRole, revokeRole, CONTROLLER, updateIntegrations), every custom error (NoAgentAdmins, NoDefaultAdmins, ZeroDefaultAdmin), the Deployment log and the return stay raw memory.
findings.rule: Treat the value of mem[64] after its last store as one symbol: v = mem[64] binds v to it and any later read of mem[64] with no intervening store to word 64 is v, so v - mem[64] folds to 0 and the existing call/error/return decoding applies, even when the stored value came out of a loop.
